column3: The ticker only retries signal delivery until the result channel fires; elapsed time never decides the assertion.
Both deadlines are fixed in the past to test cancellation propagation and never wait.
The sleeping child is the stop fixture's subject and is killed, never waited out.
The timers are failure ceilings around a real command and its forced reap; successful observation comes from the command result.
The probes observe real kernel process transitions; success is an identity fact and the delays only avoid busy-spinning.
The scans observe real kernel process membership; success is a survivor fact and the delays only avoid busy-spinning.
The sleeps only pace forced teardown of real process groups before temporary-directory removal.
The installed-process fixture succeeds on its published row, and the sleep only avoids busy-spinning while observing it.
The installed runner fixture succeeds on kernel identity and health state, and the sleeps only avoid busy-spinning while observing it.
Two sleeps keep fixture subjects alive until killed, while the third only paces observation of a real owner's kernel death.
The context is passed to a fake that checks for a deadline and returns immediately without waiting.
The timer is only a failure ceiling after a fixture custodian receives SIGKILL; success comes from Wait returning.
The ticker and deadlines bound observation of real fixture process exit states while success comes from the kernel fact.
The ticker spaces fixture writes, and all assertions count samples only after the writer reports completion.
